'''Branden Dawson''' (born February 1, 1993) is an American basketball player  who recently completed his college career for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. A native of [[Gary, Indiana]], he played for [[Lew Wallace High School]]. Upon graduation from high school, he enrolled in Michigan State to play for the Spartans. In his senior season, he helped his team reach the [[2015_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament#Final_Four|Final Four of the NCAA Tournament]]. 

==High school career==
Dawson played high school basketball for [[Lew Wallace High School|Lew Wallace]], under coach Renaldo Thomas.<ref name="nwitimes">{{cite web | url=http://www.nwitimes.com/conferences/northwestern-conference/lew-wallace-s-branden-dawson-is-a-nationally-ranked-recruit/article_880db6f4-387a-5ddd-849b-e50be2dd0718.html | title=Lew Wallace's Branden Dawson is a nationally ranked recruit | publisher=The Times of Northwest Indiana | date=November 20, 2009 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Hanlon, Steve}}</ref> He had to sit out most of his freshman season, being academically inelligible.<ref name="nwitimes" /> Dawson was selected for the [[2011 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] following his senior year.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://thehoopdoctors.com/2011/02/2011-mcdonalds-all-american-rosters-announced/ | title=2011 McDonald’s All American Rosters Announced | publisher=The Hoop Doctors | date=February 15, 2011 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Moll, Allen}}</ref>

==College career==
Following interest from several schools, receiving offers from [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] among others, Dawson verbally committed to [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] in August 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.theonlycolors.com/2010/8/4/1606040/welcome-aboard-branden-dawson | title=Welcome Aboard: Branden Dawson | publisher=SB★NATION | date=August 4, 2010 | accessdate=June 18, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/430026-spartan-hoopla-brandon-dawson-commits-to-michigan-state | title=Branden Dawson Commits to Michigan State | publisher=Bleacher Report | date=August 4, 2010 | accessdate=June 18, 2015 | author=Biggers, Adam}}</ref> He had 15 points and 9 rebounds in his first game for the Spartans, an exhibition 85–57 win against [[Ferris State University|Ferris State]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.theonlycolors.com/2011/10/31/2525734/michigan-state-85-ferris-state-58 | title=And So It Begins: Michigan State 85 - Ferris State 58 | publisher=SB★NATION | date=November 1, 2011 | accessdate=June 18, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/103011aab.html | title=Spartans Top Ferris State, 85-58, In Exhibition Opener | publisher=Michigan State Athletics | date=October 30, 2011 | accessdate=June 19, 2015}}</ref> Dawson scored 10 points in his competitive debut for Michigan State, a 67–55 loss to [[2011–12 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the 2011 [[Carrier Classic]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111111aab.html | title=MSU Falls To No.1 UNC In Carrier Classic, 67-55 | publisher=Michigan State Athletics | date=November 11, 2011 | accessdate=June 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/unc-basketball-beats-michigan-state-aboard-aircraft-carrier-uss-carl-vinson-president-barack-obama-attendance-article-1.976525 | title=UNC basketball beats Michigan State aboard aircraft carrier USS Carl Vinson with President Barack Obama in attendance | publisher=Daily News (New York) | date=November 11, 2011 | accessdate=June 19, 2015}}</ref>  His freshman season came to an end after he tore his left [[anterior cruciate ligament]], in a game against [[2011–12 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7646283/michigan-state-spartans-branden-dawson-tears-acl-year | title=Branden Dawson has torn ACL | publisher=ESPN | date=March 5, 2012 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Katz, Andy}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sbnation.com/2012/3/4/2845218/branden-dawson-injury-torn-acl-michigan-state-basketball | title=Branden Dawson Injury: Torn ACL Will End Michigan State Freshman's Season | publisher=SB★NATION | date=March 4, 2012 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Tjarks, Jonathan}}</ref> He still managed to average 8.5 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a freshman, and improved to 8.9 points and 5.9 rebounds per game as a junior.<ref name="msubio"/>

In January 2014, Dawson broke his right hand, after slamming it on a table during a film session.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2014/01/23/branden-dawson-michigan-state-broken-bone-out-4-5-weeks/4802817/ | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson out with broken bone in right hand | publisher=USA TODAY | date=January 24, 2014 | accessdate=June 18, 2015 | author=Rexrode, Joe}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2014/01/michigan_states_branden_dawson_45.html | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson breaks bone in hand, out 4-to-5 weeks | publisher=mlive.com | date=January 23, 2014 | accessdate=June 18, 2015 | author=Van Stratt, Gillian}}</ref> He posted averages11.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 28.3 minutes per game during his junior season.<ref name="msubio"/> As a senior, he was named second team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] and Big Ten All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2015/03/michigan_states_branden_dawson_69.html | title=Three Michigan State players named All-Big Ten; Branden Dawson named second-team, all-defensive team | publisher=mlive.com | date=March 9, 2015 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Austin, Kyle}}</ref> In 35 games as a senior, Dawson averaged 11.9 points, 9.1 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game.<ref name="msubio"/> He led Michigan State to the Final Four as a senior, where they lost to Duke. “This is the main reason why I chose Michigan State,” Dawson said. “It was to be part of championships and Final Fours. It means a lot what has happened over my four years here. I’m never going to forget Michigan State.”<ref>{{cite news|last1=Oren|first1=Paul|title=NBA Draft is next step for Lew Wallace grad Branden Dawson|url=http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/basketball/college/ncaa-tournament/mens-tournament/nba-draft-is-next-step-for-lew-wallace-grad-branden/article_e3b6180b-fcde-5217-a2d1-787bbaa9e0b4.html|accessdate=June 18, 2015|work=The Times of Northwest Indiana|date=April 5, 2015}}</ref>

During his four-year career at Michigan State Dawson played in 130 games. starting in 121 of them. He averaged 26.6 minutes a game. He averaged 10.1 points a game, and 6.9 Rebounds a game. Throughout his four-year career, Dawson never made a three-point shot in nine attempts.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2014-2015/histcarr.html#INDIV.FCA | title=2014–15 Individual Career History | publisher=Michigan State Athletics | accessdate=June 19, 2015}}</ref> At the time of his graduation, Dawson was Michigan State's all-time leader in blocked shots, with 142.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/mens-basketball/2015/04/09/couch-column-msu-top-fifty-additions/25483137/ | title=Valentine, Trice, Dawson belong in MSU's top 50 | publisher=Lansing State Journal | date=April 9, 2015 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Couch, Graham}}</ref>

== Personal ==

Dawson was born on February 1, 1993 to Leon Albritton and Cassandra Dawson.<ref name="msubio">{{cite web | url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/branden_dawson_771218.html | title=Branden Dawson Bio | publisher=Michigan State Athletics | accessdate=June 17, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2012/02/michigan_states_branden_dawson_1.html | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson has matured thanks to family in Gary and East Lansing | publisher=mlive.com | date=February 18, 2012 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Leung, Diamond}}</ref> On 30 March 2010, while a junior at high school, Dawson became a father, to a son named My'Shawn.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2013/02/michigan_states_branden_dawson_27.html | title=Michigan State's Branden Dawson challenged with balancing basketball, fatherhood | publisher=mlive.com | date=February 8, 2013 | accessdate=June 17, 2015 | author=Leung, Diamond}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/03/01/branden-dawson-michigan-state/24206695/ | title=MSU's Dawson finds motivation in role as father | publisher=Detroit Free Press | date=March 1, 2015 | accessdate=June 18, 2015 | author=Rexrode, Joe}}</ref> Dawson received a degree in [[sociology]] from [[Michigan State University]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2015/05/for_ex-msu_standout_branden_da.html | title=For ex-MSU standout Branden Dawson, NBA Draft Combine invitation was a godsend | publisher=mlive.com | date=May 15, 2015 | accessdate=June 9, 2015 | author=Mayo, David}}</ref>
